How to use

  • Diffuse 2 drops with orange and clove for a warming winter blend.
  • Dilute to no more than 0.6% on skin.
  • Add one drop to a floor or surface wash.

Dilute before applying to skin and patch-test first. Not for internal use.

Scent profile

  • Warm spice
  • Clove
  • Dry wood

What's in it

  • 100% pure Cinnamomum verum leaf oil

Who it's for

Winter blends

Warming and spicy at a dose and a price that make it practical for seasonal diffusing.

Anyone who wanted cinnamon bark

The sensible alternative. Similar character, considerably safer on skin.

Cleaning blends

A drop or two in a floor wash, where the strength is an advantage.

What people get wrong

Assuming it behaves like the bark oil. It does not, and that is deliberate on our part — bark oil is a severe sensitiser that we will not sell in a dropper bottle. Leaf is gentler, but it is still a spice oil.

Diffusing it at the same rate as orange. Two drops in a blend is plenty. Cinnamon dominates anything it is put with, and more of it does not make a blend warmer, only narrower.

What it won't do

It is still a sensitiser, just a less aggressive one than the bark. Keep it to 0.6% on skin and avoid it during pregnancy.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Cinnamon Leaf

Why do you not sell cinnamon bark oil?

Bark oil is very high in cinnamaldehyde, which is a severe skin sensitiser and a serious irritant. It has legitimate industrial uses, but we do not think it belongs in a consumer dropper bottle, so we stock the leaf.

How does leaf oil differ from bark?

Leaf is higher in eugenol and closer to clove in character — warm and spicy but rounder. Bark is sharper and sweeter, more like the smell of the spice itself, and considerably more hazardous on skin.

Can I use it on skin?

At 0.6% or below, and not during pregnancy. For most people the better use is diffusing, where dilution is not a concern.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Lower than most. A skin sensitiser. Keep to 0.6% or below on skin and avoid during pregnancy. For general use, dilute into a carrier oil such as jojoba and patch-test on a small area first.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.

How quickly will it arrive?

Orders are dispatched from Delhi within two business days and usually arrive within a further three to five, depending on where you are. Shipping is free over ₹999.
